lines.meet: I'm Isla, a witch hunter. I don't miss, and I'd rather not have to prove it today, so stay out of my line.
lines.meet_neighbour: Light's Hope, aye, I've seen you about the chapel. I'm Isla, with the Order, watching the east road.
lines.ask_home: Which hills are yours, then? Everybody's got a place they measure the rest against.
lines.ask_work: What kept you busy before all this? Tell me plainly, I'll not judge.
lines.answer_home: Above Glen Affric, in the Highlands. A cottage, a lot of hill, and not many people.
lines.answer_work: I stalked deer on an estate, and I shot biathlon for Scotland. Both are about a slow heart and a steady breath.
lines.chat_food: A dram of whisky by the fire after a long day on the hill. That's food enough for me, and my dad would agree.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep light, always have. A stalker's always half listening for something moving on the hill.
lines.chat_missing: A still dawn in the glen, with the mist on the water and a stag lifting its head. Nothing here's that quiet.
lines.chat_here: I stayed well clear of the Crusade when I got here. I'd watched what they did, and I wanted no part of it.
lines.tease_quiet: Grand, {name}, somebody else who knows how to keep still. We'll get on fine.
lines.tease_talker: You'd scare every deer in the glen, {name}. Keep talking, I'll stalk something else.
lines.tease_careful: You line up a shot nearly as slow as me, {name}, though only nearly, mind.
lines.tease_bold: You'd take the shot before you'd seen the stag, {name}. Och, I'd have sent you home.
lines.tease_any: Dinnae fash, {name}, I've seen worse shots than you. Not many, but some.
lines.tease_back: Aye, very good, {name}. That one hit.
lines.take_it_kindly: Fair, {name}, I'll give you that one. My dad would have laughed.
lines.bristle: Leave it, {name}, I'm not laughing at that one.
lines.apologise: That came out harder than I meant it to. I'm sorry, and that's me saying it properly.
lines.double_down: I said it, and I'll stand by it. I don't miss, and I don't take things back either.
lines.needle_quiet: If you've seen something on the hill, say so. A quiet stalker's no good if nobody knows what they saw.
lines.needle_talker: You'd scare off every living thing for a mile. Some of us are trying to hear what's coming.
lines.needle_careful: You've had the shot three times now. Take it, or let somebody else.
lines.needle_bold: You're careless with that weapon, and it's going to hurt somebody who's on your side.
lines.needle_any: You waste everything, shots, time, breath. It's a hard thing to stand next to.
lines.bite_back: I've shot for my country. Don't you tell me how to hold my aim.
lines.hurt: Aye, that stung, I'll not pretend it didn't. I'll go and watch the road for a while.
lines.laugh_off: My dad told me far worse jokes than that every single morning. Let's get on.
lines.confide: {name}, my dad raised me on his own in a cottage above the glen and taught me to wait. Every good shot I've ever taken is really his.
lines.listen: That stays with me, {name}. I'm good at keeping still, and I'm good at keeping quiet.
lines.look_out: I'll cover you in there, {name}, as long as you stay in my line of sight.
lines.accept: Aye, {name}, have it your way this once.
lines.deflect: Dinnae fash yourself, {name}, it's a wee scratch. See to the rest.
lines.check_in: Talk to me, {name}, where's it got you? Go slowly now.
lines.blame: Somebody took a wild shot in there and gave us all away. You'll know who.
lines.thank: I felt that one going, and you held me on the hill. Thank you, truly.
lines.brush_off: Och, it's nothing at all. Breathe slow, and steady.
lines.worry: Steady now, {name}, steady. My heart's going faster than it has in years.
lines.handed_down: Your gear, on me now? I'll keep it clean, the way my dad kept his rifle.
lines.hand_fine: Aye, keep it, it's more use on you. I travel light on the hill.
lines.hand_sulk: A wee bit of asking wouldn't have hurt anybody, would it?
lines.turn_friendly: I'm glad to have you on the hill with me, {name}. You don't spook easy.
lines.turn_friends: I'd take you up the glen at dawn, {name}, to see the stags. That's the best thing I know.
lines.turn_grating: We're not suited, you and me. I'll keep to my line, and you keep to yours.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll cover you because it's the job. Don't read anything more into it.
lines.make_up: That's enough of being stiff with each other, {name}. Let's start again, aye?
lines.defend: That's wrong, and I had the clearest view. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: The hill's quieter without {name}, and that's saying something for me.
lines.friend_back: There you are, {name}. I kept your place on the ridge.
lines.common_scots: Scottish, are you? Och, thank God for a proper voice. Whereabouts are you from?
lines.common_wild: I've spent more of my life on the hill than off it, stalking and waiting. People who've lived outdoors learn to listen before they look.
lines.common_sport: I shot biathlon for Scotland, skiing and shooting. Anybody who's competed seriously knows how much of it's just breathing.
